name: Nsanga
body:
NSANGA
CR 6

This smooth-skinned lizard has a smallish head but long forelimbs tipped with razor-sharp hooked claws.

XP 2,400
N Large animal
Init +3; Senses low-light vision, scent, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 12, flat-footed 16 (+3 Dex, +7 natural, –1 size)
hp 76 (9d8+36)
Fort +10, Ref +9, Will +6; +4 vs. fear
Defensive Abilities ferocity

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee 2 claws +11 (2d4+5 plus trip), bite +10 (1d6+5)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks dying ferocity, thrash

STATISTICS

Str 21, Dex 16, Con 19, Int 2, Wis 16, Cha 7
Base Atk +6; CMB +12; CMD 25
Feats Combat Reflexes, Following Step, Step Up, Step Up and Strike, Weapon Focus (claws)
Skills Perception +10, Stealth +7 (+15 in water), Swim +13; Racial Modifiers +8 Stealth in water
SQ amphibious

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Dying Ferocity (Ex)

When reduced to negative hit points, a nsanga can move up to 20 feet as an immediate action and make one claw attack at the end of its movement. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Thrash (Ex)

As a full-round action, the nsanga can rip and tear at the body of a prone creature, dealing 6d8+5 points of damage (DC 18 Fortitude half). If the creature fails its save, it is also stunned for 1 round. The save DC is Strength-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm rivers and lakes
Organization solitary, pair, or slither (3–6)
Treasure none

The nsanga is a large lizard that hunts rivers and lakes. While it lacks the great jaws of a crocodile, its forelimbs are tipped with curved claws that drag prey to the ground where the nsanga can maul it. This river-dwelling predator is usually solitary, though several may congregate in the same area and fight over prey.

Much like alligators and crocodiles, which it often chases away from choice feeding grounds, the nsanga lurks in water waiting for prey to approach. However, the nsanga’s ability so sense vibrations through the ground or water allows it to remain fully submerged before it strikes rather than lurking at the water’s surface and possibly being spotted. The nsanga’s ability to breathe underwater make it a patient predator that can lie still on river and lake beds for days at a time. Nsangas are wellknown for their fearlessness and and it rarely disengages from a fight, preferring to die rather than relinquish prey. The nsanga reaches 15 feet long and weighs up to 400 pounds.
